chapter_seo_title: Li Huowang Enters the Supervisory Heavenly Office – Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch. 377
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang loses Bai Lingmiao to the sword’s corruption, discovers a parasitic encroachment, and steps into the heart of the Supervisory Heavenly Office—home of the Mohists.
og_description: Li Huowang faces his worst fear: Bai Lingmiao’s accusation that he loved a fantasy, not her. Then the Mohists enter the stage.
twitter_title: Corrupted Bai Lingmiao leaves Li Huowang, and the Mohists appear in the Supervisory Heavenly Office
twitter_description: Li Huowang learns there are two kinds of Mohist schools—and not all of them are safe.

lore_anchors.definition: A government-sponsored supernormal law enforcement body; it monitors supernatural activity and enforces imperial order over occult matters, operating with near-total autonomy.
One of the Hundred Schools of Thought from ancient China, emphasizing universal love, merit, and engineering. In the Dao-Twisted World, it has split into two branches: Qi Mo (齐墨) and Liang Mo (梁墨).

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Bai Lingmiao suddenly become hostile?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The Purple-Tasseled Sword’s killing-intent corruption is overwriting her personality, making her aggressive, blunt, and dismissive of Li Huowang.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is the difference between Qi Mo and Liang Mo?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Qi Mo is the “orthodox” branch accepted by the Supervisory Heavenly Office, while Liang Mo is considered heretical and potentially dangerous.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Does Li Huowang succeed in defying fate?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Not yet, but his defiant attitude at dawn signals he is not giving up—despite the mounting pressure from Li Sui’s takeover.
